# Independent measure audit: intrinsic finite-base own-depth upper bound

Primary source:
`candidate 04819028a2421217`.
Dependency read in full:
`candidate 4e07416b95553009`.

**Result: PASS.** The upper bound D_S(z,y)<=N f_z(y) is proved for the
stated intrinsic H_q measure and does not assert an OC lower bound.

## Measure and zero-dimensional cases

Boundedness gives finitely many nonempty integer fibers. A nonempty compact
convex fiber has Hausdorff dimension equal to its affine dimension, so the
Hausdorff dimension of their finite union is the largest such dimension.
Exactly the q-dimensional fibers have positive finite H_q measure; their
embeddings into distinct integer fibers are isometric and disjoint.
Finite additivity therefore gives the displayed fiber-sum identity with
positive finite total mass. Lower-dimensional fibers contribute exactly
zero to every measured cap.

At q=0 each nonempty convex fiber is a singleton. H_0 is counting measure,
N counts all fibers, and the separately stated f_z=1 convention gives the
trivial upper bound D_S<=N. The relative boundary of a singleton in its
own affine hull is empty. No nonexistent zero-dimensional normal or 0^0
expression is used. If n=0, a smaller-than-q nonempty source fiber cannot
exist because there is only one base.

## Lower-dimensional source locations

If a base z0 of a smaller-dimensional fiber belonged to conv(P_q), an
actual positive-weight Minkowski combination of maximal-dimensional fibers
would lie in K_z0. Fixing all but one summand exhibits a q-dimensional
subset, contradicting the source's lower dimension. Thus z0 lies outside
the compact convex hull of positive-measure bases. Strict separation gives
a closed ambient halfspace using only integer-coordinate directions that
contains the whole source fiber and misses every positive-measure fiber.
Its H_q mass is zero. The separator's coefficients need not be integers;
only its coordinate block is the integer-variable block, which is all that
the statement requires.

## Generic directions and changing affine planes

For q>=1 each E_z is a nonzero q-dimensional direction space, so E_z^perp
is a proper linear subspace of R^d. A finite union of these subspaces has
empty interior; generic normals simultaneously nonconstant on every
positive-measure fiber approximate any desired source intrinsic normal.
Every associated fiber hyperplane is then at most (q-1)-dimensional and
has zero H_q mass, including at supporting levels. Tails are continuous,
and strictly decreasing between support levels by positive relative
interior volume in every such open slab.

For a barycentric combination of constrained bases returning to z0, all
positive-weight captured bodies have q-volume t>0 and therefore full
direction space E_z. The actual Minkowski combination lies in K_z0.
Fixing every other summand shows that a translate of a positive homothetic
copy of each captured body lies in K_z0. Hence E_z is contained in E_z0;
equality of dimensions makes these spaces equal. This is a consequence
for each relevant dependency, not a global assertion that all fibers have
parallel planes.

After translating each of these parallel planes into E_z0, intrinsic
q-volume is unchanged. Their Minkowski combination translates by the
corresponding barycentric combination of translation vectors. Its affine
plane is that of K_z0 because it has full q-dimension and lies in K_z0.
Ordinary q-dimensional BM therefore applies with the same Euclidean
normalization, and gives captured-combination mass at least t. No arbitrary
change of integer coordinates or untracked Jacobian is present.

## Quantile majorants and their finite Farkas dependency

Only fibers of total mass greater than t require proper t-quantiles.
The source is among them. Every positive-weight dependence among their
base displacement vectors can be normalized to a convex combination
returning to z0; the preceding BM argument gives its exact quantile
inequality. The finite affine-majorant lemma then supplies the required
single integer-coordinate slope b.

The dependency's proof of that lemma is sound: conic supports reduce to
linearly independent subsets, so the finitely generated cone is closed;
projection of (0,1) onto that closed convex cone separates it with a
strictly positive final coordinate, furnishing b. The same argument works
when n=0. Unconstrained positive-measure fibers have whole mass at most t;
lower-dimensional fibers have zero mass. Therefore no omitted constraint
can increase the cap bound beyond Nt.

## Source boundary limits and attainment

The source intrinsic depth is attained on its own direction sphere because
cap volume is continuous and that sphere is compact. Opposite caps sum to
the source volume: their shared boundary has zero H_q mass. Thus any
positive minimizing source cap is proper and strictly subtotal. Approaching
its normal by generic ambient vectors preserves its mass by dominated
convergence and keeps its threshold through the fixed source point.

For zero own depth, lowering each approximating threshold below u_l.y by
a positive epsilon_l makes the source cap positive: y belongs to the
source, and the level is strictly below its maximum. Dominated convergence
makes these cap masses tend to zero, so they are also strictly subtotal
for all sufficiently large l. Each resulting ambient halfspace contains
the same original source point. Taking only numerical infima and limits
of cap masses proves D_S=0; neither a limiting point nor a limiting
integer slope is needed.

A relative-boundary point has zero own depth by an intrinsic supporting
hyperplane. Conversely a maximal-dimensional fiber centroid has positive
mixed depth from its own fiber alone. If an ambient trace has nonzero
restriction to that affine plane, ordinary q-dimensional Gruenbaum applies;
if the restriction vanishes, containing the centroid means containing the
entire source fiber. This proves the stated existence of positive-depth
locations without claiming any fraction of the total OC mass.

No correction to either read source is needed for this extension.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
